scope: Nine full image mockups followed by editable SVG reconstruction; Home remains the visual reference.

shared.visualReference: The approved Home image, including its depth, illustrated motifs, button treatments and navigation hierarchy. Do not use the rejected generated SVGs as the visual reference.
shared.chrome: Preserve existing Forge brand, page navigation, active-page highlight, live token/pass indicators and close controls. Arcade and Runway are modal destinations with their own close/back navigation.
shared.defaultMockup: Show an established player's Simple Mode desktop state. Advanced and conditional controls below remain reachable in their existing mode/tab/state; they do not all need to be expanded in one default image.
shared.liveMedia: Generated accessories, catalog thumbnails, avatar viewports, player portraits and generated graphics remain live content slots. Concept artwork may illustrate these slots in the mockup, but must not become permanent sample items or fake player data in the game.
shared.prices: Use symbolic live-price labels in the specifications. Generation prices come from app.state.prices, refreshed through MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync and CommerceService:GetPrices; Config SuggestedPrice is a fallback. Roblox purchase/creation prompts determine the final external charge.
shared.editableSvg: Use separate named groups for each panel, button, icon and field. Keep labels as editable SVG text. Keep live media and dynamic values replaceable. Do not hide the entire mockup inside one raster image element.
shared.responsive: Allow native scrolling for collections, galleries and overflow settings. Preserve compact single-column/list-detail flows, keyboard focus, high contrast, reduced motion and readable text. Do not crop secondary actions to force the mockup to fit.

screens.title: Create UGC
screens.purpose: Describe a new accessory, confirm its cost, then generate a private 3D creation to fit and wear.
screens.composition: Make the prompt composer the large left focal panel, with a generous multiline field, a row of illustrated idea chips, a quiet helper strip and a prominent priced generation button. Put latest creation/reference preview and progress in a narrower right rail. Keep payment and balance controls distinct from the main action. Decorative 3D accessory art can connect this to Home without masquerading as a completed user item.

Five existing idea chips: Dragon Wings, Crystal Crown, Neon Katana, Steampunk Hat, Fairy Wings
Generate / retry-credit action with live Robux or ad-token cost
HOW IT WORKS guide control and access to Advanced Mode / more creation methods
Payment choice: Robux or Tokens; token balance; optional rewarded-ad action; buy token pack
Latest creation progress/status and its existing native follow-up controls
secondaryControls: Method choices: Direct Forge, Art-Directed, Upload Reference, My Avatar
Advanced style presets and fit-region selection; detail density is fixed BALANCED and has no picker
Art-Directed quality tiers Low/Medium/High; reference image; Approve & build and reroll
Upload Reference Roblox Image/Decal ID field and one-time CustomImageUpload unlock when needed
My Avatar view choices: Headshot, Bust, Full body; optional styling notes
Priority Pass purchase/use action when available
Existing queue-slot information, daily check-in calendar, daily quests and conditional onboarding guide

profile.tokens and profile.bonusTokens; generation-eligible balance stays distinct from free reward tokens
profile.retryCredits, current jobs, reference asset, queue progress and benefit ownership

state.prices.CustomImageUpload, PriorityPass and TokenPack70

guardrails: Do not add a Save, Download or Publish button to the default prompt composer; fitting/publishing belongs in My Items.
A reference image and its conversion are separate paid stages. Do not imply one generation price includes Roblox publication.
Rewarded ads remain optional and disabled/unavailable states remain visible.

screens.title: My Items
screens.purpose: Select an owned creation, inspect its live avatar fit, equip it in this game or publish a wearable through Roblox.
screens.composition: Use a tall collection rail on the left and a larger inspection stage on the right. Give the selected item name and status a clear header; make the live avatar/model preview dominant; place fit readiness and equip/publish actions beneath it. Advanced editing belongs in an expandable or scrollable lower region, not across the avatar.

Live selected-item avatar viewport, drag/zoom interaction, reset camera and conditional Retry preview
Fit/texture readiness status
Equip in game / Remove and Publish wearable actions with their actual disabled/busy states
Advanced Mode access; empty collection action Create your first accessory

Save fit and Reset fit
Named fit presets: save, apply, delete
Named saved outfits: save current outfit, wear outfit, delete saved outfit
Original-item title/description fields and Save details

selectedItemId, fitDrafts and equippedItemIds

Original listing price is selected.listingPriceRobux; equip and fit changes have no generation charge
guardrails: Do not replace a user's selected accessory with decorative sample content.
Publish, share publicly and list for sale are distinct actions with different eligibility.

screens.title: Market
screens.purpose: Browse community-created accessories, inspect them, try them on and optionally buy a personal copy.
screens.composition: Place a wide search field and Search button above a clean three-card discovery grid, with a persistent live avatar preview beside it. Each card needs a large real item image, title, creator, ownership price where relevant, free Try on action and separate like/favorite controls. Keep browsing filters visually quieter than item art.

Top Creators leaderboard and existing Plus benefit control where enabled
Conditional first-look journey/guide controls
Item detail overlay with its original purchase/try/social actions

Each item's real image, ownerName, listingPriceRobux, likes/favorites and viewer selections
Current live avatar and actual equipped/try-on state

guardrails: Do not add invented category tabs, sale discounts or a shopping cart.
Do not depict free preview as ownership or bake sample prices/creator names into production art.

screens.title: Avatar Lab
screens.purpose: Try real Roblox catalog items for free, build a mixed catalog/custom look and save it.
screens.composition: Use a catalog workspace on the left and a generous live-avatar stage on the right. Keep Find items / My avatar tabs near the header, search above category chips, and spacious real item cards below. Each card clearly separates free Try on from Buy / view in Roblox. The avatar stage should feel like Home's polished character pedestal while remaining a live viewport.

guardrails: Do not conflate this catalog styling workspace with AI generation.
Do not label Save in Forge as a Roblox avatar purchase or permanent catalog ownership.

screens.title: Avatar Graphics
screens.purpose: Generate a standalone 2D image from the player's avatar or a text prompt, then manage the image gallery.
screens.composition: Make a large artistic composer on the left, with From My Avatar / Text Prompt source buttons, multiline prompt and a prominent live-priced Create action. Use the right rail for actual in-progress status and a scrollable personal image gallery. Put Create / Discover tabs above the panels. Illustrative art should emphasize images rather than wearable 3D accessories.

screens.title: Games
screens.purpose: Choose one of the three existing free play destinations while creations continue building.
screens.composition: Create three equally clear illustrated destination cards across the content area, each with a distinctive themed illustration, short benefit text and one large action: Arcade, Forge Runway, AFK Token Lounge. Use the approved Home depth and visual energy rather than a generic dashboard of many tiny tiles.
requiredControls: Open Arcade
Open Forge Runway
Enter AFK Token Lounge
Existing navigation/close controls
liveData: Arcade mini-game count from Config.Arcade.Games
Existing queued creations continue independently of this destination screen
priceSources: All three destinations are free to open
Rewards and AFK grants come from Config/authoritative player state; rewarded ads remain optional
guardrails: Do not add unsupported games, daily spin, battle pass, loot box or match-making controls.
Do not imply every game automatically grants a fixed spendable token payout per play.

screens.title: Arcade
screens.purpose: Launch a real mini-game or inspect weekly game leaderboards and personal bests.
screens.composition: Use a dedicated full modal frame with a prominent Arcade title, readable weekly-prize strip and a balanced 4-by-3 grid containing the eleven games plus Leaderboard. Every game tile gets a recognizable illustration/icon, real name, brief description, personal-best slot, daily target where present and Play control. Keep Close clearly separate from tile art; scrolling may handle smaller screens.

Play on each of the eleven game tiles

Tile-wide activation remains available

Back to game picker from leaderboard/game view
Existing GameShell play/restart/in-game controls; mockup depicts the picker rather than a fabricated game round

GetArcadeLeaderboard and GetFriendArcadeLeaderboard results; real self score/rank

Personal best and rank are live fields, not invented score examples used as permanent UI art.

screens.title: Forge Runway
screens.purpose: Join a live themed style round, lock in a look, inspect entrants and vote when eligible.
screens.composition: Create a dedicated Runway modal with theme/phase/timer across a spacious header. Arrange entrant lineup on the left, a dominant selected-player live avatar stage in the center, and weekly spotlight on the right. Put phase instructions and primary join/lock action near the avatar, with Avatar Lab and Invite friends controls reachable below. Separate all headings from dynamic instruction rows; long lineups and conditional journey/activity content scroll.

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: Adjust creation mode, accessibility and audio; inspect equipped items, achievements and community actions.
screens.composition: Use two balanced columns of clear titled panels. Left: Create Mode, Accessibility, Audio. Right: Equipped Now, Achievements and community actions. Settings should share Home's polish through restrained illustrated accents and confident controls, with enough spacing for explanatory copy. Keep the full achievements and equipped lists scrollable rather than showing a fixed sample set.
